lede.s: Living in North Carolina is one of UNC's top-tier factors. Out of state, about 1 in 10 got in. So if you're applying from outside NC, the rest of this page is where you win.

grids.aria: 37 of 100 dots filled: 37% of North Carolina applicants were admitted
About 10 of 100 dots filled: 9.6% of out-of-state applicants were admitted

chances.src: Fall 2025 first-years (C1): NC 6,605 of 17,846 admitted (37.0%). Out of state 4,685 of 48,645 (9.6%). International 1,461 of 9,756 (15.0%). Overall 12,751 of 76,247 (16.7%).

ladder.title: 7 things are top-tier. Your GPA is one step down.
ladder.lede: That doesn't mean grades don't matter. How hard your classes are is still top-tier. UNC wants to see the whole person.
considered: First in your family to go to college
not_considered: How often you toured or emailed
ladder.note: Top tier = where your hours go before Jan 15 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set.

numbers.lede: Type your weighted GPA to see where it sits next to UNC's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.default: Average weighted GPA of enrolled first-years: 4.47.
gpa.near: Right around UNC's average. Now your top-tier rows decide it: classes, essay, letters, activities.
gpa.above: Above UNC's average. Good start. GPA is one step down here, so your top-tier rows still do the heavy lifting.
gpa.below: Below UNC's average. That's not a no. At UNC, your classes, essay, letters and activities are all rated above GPA. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of first-years who reported a class rank were in the top 10% of their class.

money.title: If you qualify for aid, UNC says it covers all of your need.
money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. The net price calculator gives your family a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: About 3 in 10 first-years get need-based grants. The average need-based package is $21,695 a year.
money.src: Sections G1 and H2, 2025–26 Common Data Set. Tuition and required fees only; housing and food cost extra.

todo.title: 4 moves, all aimed at UNC's top tier.

items.title: List your hardest classes.
items.body: Honors, AP, IB, dual enrollment. Make sure every one shows up on your application.

items.title: Read your essay out loud.
items.body: If a sentence could be about anyone, cut it. It's the only essay UNC asks for this year, and essays are top-tier here.

items.title: Put a number on every activity.
items.body: Hours a week, people you led, what changed because of you.

items.title: NC students: do your residency step.
items.body: It's separate from the Common App and due Feb 21. Residency is top-tier at UNC, so do it the week you apply. Easy to miss.

todo.done: All 4 done. That's a real application. ✓

title.s: Is your essay doing its job?
title.p: Is your student's essay doing its job?

lede.s: Essays are top-tier at UNC, and this year your Common App essay is the only one it asks for. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read your essay, then tap what's true.
lede.p: Essays are top-tier at UNC, and this year the Common App essay is the only one it asks for. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read your student's essay together, then tap what's true.

items.title: It answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the prompt. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only one person could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows one real moment.
items.body: A scene beats a list of awards. The list already lives in the activities section.

items.title: A reader could sum it up in one line.
items.body: Readers spend a few minutes per file. Hand them the sentence they'll repeat when they argue for you.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own essay.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge an essay you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: Your essay's job is to make one reader fight for you. At UNC, your essays, letters and activities are all top-tier. Give that reader three places to find the same person.
